facts.statement: Zarafasaura is classified as a genus within the family Elasmosauridae.
Zarafasaura belongs to the family Elasmosauridae.
The genus Zarafasaura was first named in 2011 by a team including Peggy Vincent and Nathalie Bardet.
facts.quote: Zarafasaura was first named by Peggy Vincent, Nathalie Bardet, Xabier Pereda Suberbiola, Baâdi Bouya, Mbarek Amaghzaz and Saïd Meslouh in 2011

facts.statement: Fossils of Zarafasaura have been found in the Ouled Abdoun Basin of Morocco.
facts.quote: Zarafasaura is an extinct genus of elasmosaurid known from the Ouled Abdoun Basin of Morocco

facts.statement: Zarafasaura was a relatively small elasmosaur measuring approximately 3 to 4 meters in length and weighing about 100 kilograms.
facts.quote: As a relatively small elasmosaur, it would have measured around 3 - 4 m long and weighed about 100 kg

facts.statement: The holotype specimen, OCP-DEK/GE 315, consists of an articulated but incomplete and crushed skull and mandible.
facts.quote: The holotype of Zarafasaura, OCP-DEK/GE 315, consists of an articulated incomplete dorsoventrally crushed skull and mandible

facts.statement: A second specimen found in 2013 included a more complete skull and previously unknown postcranial elements like forefins and vertebrae.
facts.quote: In 2013, a second specimen, WDC CMC-01, was found to have a more complete skull with previously unknown postcranial elements such as the forefins, hindfins, vertebrae, pectoral and pelvic material

facts.statement: A Zarafasaura specimen valued at €450,000 was halted from auction in Paris in 2017 and returned to Morocco.
facts.quote: In 2017, a specimen of Zarafasaura oceanis was about to be auctioned off at Hôtel Drouot (Paris). The auction house valued it at about €450,000 but the sale was halted and the specimen ultimately returned to Morocco

facts.statement: Zarafasaura is one of the last known plesiosaurs and the first elasmosaurid described from Africa.
facts.quote: Es uno de los últimos plesiosaurios conocidos, y el primer elasmosáurido descrito de África

facts.statement: Like other elasmosaurids, Zarafasaura had a long neck, a flattened body, and four limbs modified into flippers.
facts.quote: Como otros elasmosáuridos, Zarafasaura poseía un cuello bastante alargado, un cuerpo aplanado y cuatro extremidades convertidas en aletas

facts.statement: The skull of Zarafasaura appears to have been shorter than that of similar forms.
facts.quote: El cráneo también parece haber sido más corto que el de otras formas similares

facts.statement: Unique features of Zarafasaura suggest a degree of endemism among Maastrichtian plesiosaurs.
facts.quote: las características peculiares de Zarafasaura indican que había un cierto grado de endemismo entre los plesiosaurios del Maastrichtiano

facts.statement: Zarafasaura lived during the Maastrichtian stage, between 72.2 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)
